idea.working_title: Cleopatra is closer to the iPhone than to the pyramids
idea.premise: Three true timeline overlaps that make history feel impossible, each bigger than the last.
idea.payoff: T. rex lived closer in time to you than to Stegosaurus.
idea.target_audience: 16-34 curiosity-driven scrollers who follow history, science and 'mind-blown' fact accounts; broad global appeal, strong in US/UK/EU and MENA
idea.fact_basis: Great Pyramid c. 2560 BC (Khufu); Cleopatra VII 69-30 BC; first iPhone 2007; Wrangel Island mammoths to c. 4,000 years ago; teaching at Oxford by 1096; Tenochtitlan founded c. 1325; Stegosaurus c. 155-145 Ma; T. rex c. 68-66 Ma.

beats.voiceover: Cleopatra is closer to iPhones than pyramids.
beats.open_loop: How can that possibly be true?

beats.voiceover: The Great Pyramid was already twenty-five centuries old when she was born. To her, it was ancient history.
beats.open_loop: If the pyramid was ancient to Cleopatra, what else was alive when it was built?

beats.voiceover: But here's what breaks your brain. When the pyramid's first stones were laid, something else was still walking the Earth.
beats.open_loop: What was still walking the Earth?

beats.voiceover: Woolly mammoths. A small population survived on an Arctic island until about four thousand years ago, after the pyramid was finished.
beats.open_loop: And that's not even the strangest overlap.

beats.voiceover: Oxford University was already teaching students two centuries before the Aztecs founded Tenochtitlan.
beats.open_loop: The last one is on a completely different scale.

beats.voiceover: Now zoom out. Way out. Past humans. Past mammoths. All the way to dinosaurs.
beats.open_loop: Which dinosaur is closer to you than to its own 'neighbour'?

beats.voiceover: Tyrannosaurus rex lived closer in time to you than to Stegosaurus. About eighty million years apart. Sixty-six from you.
beats.on_screen_caption: T. REX → YOU < T. REX → STEGOSAURUS

beats.voiceover: Send this to someone who thinks history is boring. Follow for part two.
beats.on_screen_caption: SEND THIS TO A HISTORY HATER 👇

script.music_mood: Tense, cinematic ticking-clock underscore that swells into an epic, awe-struck reveal
script.music_notes: 90-100 BPM pulse with a clock-tick motif. Hard cut to silence at 15.0s for the mammoth reveal, rebuild with low brass at 22s, full drop exactly on 'Tyrannosaurus' at 35.0s, fade under the CTA and end on the same tick as frame 1 so the loop is seamless.

sound_effects.effect: T. rex roar layered with sub-bass boom
Soft pop on the send-arrow caption

editing_instructions: Frame 1 is already mid-action: no fade-in, no logo.
Cuts every 2-4 s; faster (2 s) in HOOK and FINAL_SURPRISE.
Word-by-word bold white captions with yellow highlight on numbers and names, centred in the upper third (clear of UI).
Animated gold timeline overlay at 2-8 s showing Pyramid, Cleopatra, iPhone with the gaps counting up.
Freeze-frame + 1.2x punch-in at 15.0 s on the mammoth; hold 0.3 s of silence.
Split-screen at 18-22 s: mammoth herd (left) / finished pyramid (right).
Speed-ramp the zoom-out at 29-35 s; reverse time-lapse feel.
Final frame matches frame 1 (Cleopatra + iPhone) for a seamless rewatch loop.
Colour: teal shadows, amber highlights; keep skin tones natural.
script.cta: Send this to someone who thinks history is boring. Follow for part two.

claims.statement: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built c. 2560 BC for Pharaoh Khufu.
claims.support: Egyptological consensus (4th Dynasty); Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Pyramids of Giza'.

claims.statement: Cleopatra VII (69-30 BC) lived ~2,500 years after the Great Pyramid and ~2,040 years before the first iPhone (2007).
claims.support: Cleopatra's dates per Britannica; iPhone launched by Apple in June 2007. 2560 BC to 69 BC is ~2,490 years.

claims.statement: Woolly mammoths survived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago, i.e. after the Great Pyramid was built.
claims.support: Vartanyan et al., Nature 362 (1993); Dehasque et al., Cell (2024) - last population c. 4,000 years BP.

claims.statement: Teaching at Oxford existed by 1096; the Aztecs founded Tenochtitlan c. 1325.
claims.support: University of Oxford official history page; Tenochtitlan's traditional founding date 1325 (Britannica).

claims.statement: Stegosaurus lived c. 155-145 million years ago; T. rex c. 68-66 million years ago - roughly 80 million years apart, vs 66 million years from today.
claims.support: Late Jurassic Morrison Formation dating for Stegosaurus; Late Maastrichtian for T. rex (Natural History Museum, London).
